Class RhythmNet

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.RhythmNet
final class RhythmNet extends Object
A memory of the last 3.2 seconds for the acting network (Config.rhythmNet): a causal temporal convolution (TCN: Bai, Kolter and Koltun 2018; WaveNet, van den Oord et al. 2016) over the opponent reader's window (OpponentReader.Window: 32 samples of two ticks, oldest first, ten numbers each: distance, in sight, moving away and up, both swords, hits either way, the knockback, time in the fight). Four layers of H channels, kernel K, dilations 1, 2, 4 and 8, so the newest sample sees the 30 before it (3 seconds; the oldest one only through the mean); out comes what the last layer makes of the newest sample and its mean over the window. The acting network takes that into its trunk and into the crit and escape models through weights that start at zero, so a network plays as before until it learns to use it, and it is learned from the policy's own gradient (the reader is taught only to name the opponent, and a one-frame network cannot see a rhythm).

Gemini's review, 23 October (Part 2, option A): a 1.9 fight is a 12.5-tick cycle of two swords, and a spacer that crits and holds S, a stander at 3.3 blocks and a timer that jumps on its cooldown look alike in one frame; a window needs no backpropagation through time, so the shuffled minibatches stay as they are. The user, 23 October: build it.
